title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 156 (Director to intimate Director Identification Number)

content.overview: Section 156 requires every existing director to intimate his Director Identification Number to the company or companies in which he is a director within the prescribed period of receipt of the DIN from the Central Government.
content.glance: Existing director must intimate DIN to each company where he is a director within the prescribed period after receiving the DIN.
content.study: Every existing director shall, within the prescribed period of receipt of the Director Identification Number from the Central Government, intimate his Director Identification Number to the company or all companies wherein he is a director. The director’s intimation duty is distinct from the company’s duty under section 157 to inform the Registrar. Current-law framing: identify existing director; confirm DIN received; check intimation to each company within prescribed period.

sections.heading: Who Must Intimate
sections.body: Every existing director who has received a DIN from the Central Government.

sections.heading: To Whom
sections.body: The company or all companies in which the person is a director.

sections.heading: Time
sections.body: Within the prescribed period of receipt of the DIN.

sections.heading: Link to Company Filing
sections.body: After intimation, the company informs the Registrar under section 157. The two duties are sequential and separate.

provisions.title: Director to intimate Director Identification Number

examples.title: Intimation to multiple companies
examples.body: A person is a director of three companies and receives a DIN. Under s. 156 the person must intimate the DIN to each of those three companies within the prescribed period.

examples.title: Director duty vs company duty
examples.body: The director intimates the company under s. 156; the company then files with the Registrar under s. 157. Failure of one does not automatically discharge the other.

hypotheticals.question: If the director fails to intimate the company, is the company still bound to inform the ROC under s. 157?
hypotheticals.analysis: The duties are separate. Section 156 binds the director; section 157 binds the company once it has the information. Practical compliance usually requires the director’s intimation first.

distinctions.title: Director to intimate DIN (s. 156) vs company to inform ROC (s. 157)
distinctions.left: Director’s duty to tell the company
distinctions.right: Company’s duty to tell the Registrar

misconceptions.trap: Intimating one company is enough even if the person is a director of several companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 156 requires intimation to the company or all companies wherein the person is a director.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 156 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify existing director and DIN receipt. II. Check intimation to each company within prescribed period. III. Distinguish company filing under s. 157. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: DIN receipt; companies of directorship; intimation facts; precise relief.

examTips: Separate from company’s ROC filing under s. 157.
